chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who prays behind one whose prayer is not followed, and the Imam recites aloud. He said, 'Recite for yourself, and if you do not hear yourself, there is no harm.' And that which indicates what we mentioned regarding the impermissibility of relying solely on the recitation of one whose prayer is not followed is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الِاقْتِصَارُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ: Relying solely on the recitation of (the Imam)
key_terms.مَنْ لَا يَقْتَدِي بِصَلَاتِهِ: One whose prayer is not followed (invalid or distinct prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do with their recitation when praying behind an Imam whose prayer is not followed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that when praying behind an Imam whose prayer is not validly followed (man la yuqtada bi-salatihi), the worshipper must independently recite Surah Al-Fatihah, as the Imam's recitation does not suffice for them. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the validity of the individual's prayer depends on their own fulfillment of obligatory acts, particularly recitation, rather than merely following the Imam's actions. The text further supports this by referencing other narrations that prohibit relying solely on the recitation of one who is not a valid model for imitation.
